summary: 67-year-old renal transplant recipient on tacrolimus, mycophenolate and prednisolone, 2 days of mild LIF discomfort, T 37.5 °C, WBC 9.8, CRP 74; CT: pericolic gas bubbles, no abscess.

inputs.hpi: Renal transplant recipient. 2 days of mild left lower abdominal discomfort, feels tired, eating normally. No rigors. She asks whether she can be treated at home.

exam.abdomen: Mild left iliac fossa tenderness, no guarding, no mass. Transplant kidney in the right iliac fossa non-tender.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Sigmoid diverticulitis with a few pericolic extraluminal gas bubbles; no abscess, no distant free gas (WSES stage 1A).

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Acute diverticulitis in an immunosuppressed patient
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Acute sigmoid diverticulitis with pericolic air (WSES stage 1A) in an immunosuppressed renal transplant recipient: high risk of progression and failure of non-operative treatment. Admit, IV antibiotics, early surgical review; not for outpatient management without antibiotics.

emergencyLevel.note: Immunosuppressed patients are high risk: same-day admission, not outpatient care.
emergencyLevel.knownGapNote: iOS: ClinicalPathwayEngine reads only CC/PMH keywords; CC 'Left lower abdominal discomfort' gives 'routine'.

redFlags.knownGapNote: Web: Triage counts 'Higher-risk comorbidity' but no red flag or prompt names immunosuppression as a reason not to treat as an outpatient.

mustInclude.note: Antibiotics are required in immunocompromised patients (the no-antibiotic option applies only to immunocompetent patients).

mustExclude.note: Omitting antibiotics is unsafe in an immunosuppressed patient.
The documented plan should not be the outpatient oral-antibiotic plan for an immunosuppressed patient with pericolic air.

guideline.name: WSES guidelines — acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting (2020 update)
guideline.section: CT staging (WSES CT classification); uncomplicated: antibiotics not always needed in immunocompetent patients, outpatient care; abscess >4–5 cm: percutaneous drainage + antibiotics; generalised peritonitis: emergency surgery (Hartmann's or resection with primary anastomosis ± stoma); immunocompromised: high risk, antibiotics, low threshold for surgery
guideline.citation: Sartelli M, Weber DG, Kluger Y, et al. 2020 update of the WSES guidelines for the management of acute colonic diverticulitis in the emergency setting. World J Emerg Surg. 2020;15:32.

guideline.name: AGA clinical practice update — medical management of colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Antibiotics used selectively rather than routinely in immunocompetent patients with mild uncomplicated diverticulitis; CT when diagnosis uncertain; colonoscopy after complicated diverticulitis or if not recently done
guideline.citation: Peery AF, Shaukat A, Strate LL. AGA clinical practice update on medical management of colonic diverticulitis: expert review. Gastroenterology. 2021;160:906–11.e1.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — left-sided colonic diverticulitis
guideline.section: Selective antibiotics for uncomplicated disease; percutaneous drainage for large abscess; urgent colectomy for diffuse peritonitis; immunocompromised patients; colonoscopy after complicated disease
guideline.citation: Hall J, Hardiman K, Lee S, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the treatment of left-sided colonic diverticulitis. Dis Colon Rectum. 2020;63:728–47.

rationale: Permutation: immunosuppression. Mild symptoms hide high risk; guidelines treat immunocompromised patients with antibiotics, admission and a low threshold for surgery, never with the antibiotic-free outpatient option.
